title: A stalled submission is retried, not fatal — herdr calls an agent ready before its TUI takes input
action: The last failure standing, and the plainest. D1 made herdr's `agent_prompt_stalled` a hard `DeliveryError::Stalled` that kills the run on the first occurrence. D6 narrows that: a stall proves the submission had not landed AT THAT INSTANT, not that it never will. Measured live 2026-08-21 — a worker got a fresh 173x50 tab pane, agy booted and fully drawn, bee's submission came back `agent_prompt_stalled` (`agent prompt produced no observed state change within 5000 ms; status is idle`) and the run died as `spawn_failed`; the IDENTICAL `herdr agent prompt <job> <pointer> --wait --until working --timeout 20000` typed by hand seconds afterwards on that same pane returned `agent_status: working` immediately and the worker ran to a written result. Width was not the cause — this pane was the widest in the session. The cause is the window the pre-existing code comment already named: herdr's ready flags fire before some agents accept input. Change: in `deliver_pointer`, a stalled reply joins the SAME bounded retry the ready-with-no-ack path already uses instead of returning early. Sleep the existing backoff, resend the idempotent pointer, and keep going under the two bounds already there — `DELIVERY_RESEND_ATTEMPTS` and `ACK_WAIT_BUDGET_SECS`. Only when a bound is exhausted is it terminal, and then the error must say that EVERY submission stalled, distinct from the existing never-acked wording, so the reader can tell 'the agent never took the text' from 'the agent took it and never acked'. `DeliveryError::Blocked` and `DeliveryError::Transport` stay immediate, unchanged. Keep the ack-or-result receipt exactly as D4 left it — a retry is never evidence of delivery, the ack still decides. Check the ack and result files between attempts as the loop already does, so a worker that accepted an earlier submission and is writing its ack is never resent into needlessly. Update the doc comment that currently states the stall is a hard failure, citing D6, and update the tests that pin that behaviour: a stall followed by a successful send must deliver; a stall every time must exhaust a bound and produce the every-submission-stalled message; blocked and transport must still be immediate.

truths: A stalled submission is retried under the existing bounds instead of ending the run
A stall on every attempt ends as a terminal error whose wording is distinct from the never-acked one
blocked and transport errors are still immediate
The ack or result file is still the only evidence of delivery
